title: Chocolate-Dipped Strawberries
subtitle: plump strawberries in a crisp chocolate shell with a white chocolate drizzle
imageAlt: Glossy chocolate-dipped strawberries with white chocolate drizzle on a cream plate beside a navy napkin

beforeYouStart.text: The berries must be completely dry or the chocolate will seize and slide off.
Melt the chocolate slowly in short bursts; it burns easily.

items.name: strawberries
items.note: about 16, with green tops, washed and dried completely

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Wash the strawberries, then dry them very well on paper towel and leave 15 minutes to air-dry. Line a tray with parchment.

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Microwave the chocolate and oil in a small bowl in 30-second bursts, stirring each time, until almost melted; stir until smooth.

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Holding the green top, dip each berry, let the extra drip off and lay it on the parchment.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Chill 20 minutes until the chocolate is firm.

fixIt.fix: It seized from water or heat; stir in 1 tsp more oil, or start again with fresh chocolate.
Let more drip off and scrape the bottom on the bowl's rim.
They sat too long in the fridge; make them the same day.

saleTip: Strawberries are pricey in February; the 1 lb clamshell at No Frills is usually the best deal.
swap: Milk or dark chocolate. Banana chunks or pretzels for berries.
leftovers: Eat the same day; they weep after a day in the fridge.
doneness: No cooking; melt the chocolate gently and keep it below about 45°C (115°F) so it stays glossy.
source: Based on tested chocolate-dipped strawberry methods (Food Network, Canadian Living): dry berries, microwave-melted chocolate with a little oil, chilled to set.
prepAhead: Make up to 6 hours ahead and keep in the fridge.

basic.note: The chocolate on its own, no oil: a thicker shell.

stepNotes.1: Basic: melt the chocolate on its own.

fancy.note: A white chocolate drizzle and pink sprinkles.

addSteps.title: Drizzle
addSteps.text: Once the dark chocolate is set, melt the white chocolate in 20-second bursts, drizzle it over the berries with a fork, add sprinkles and chill 10 minutes more.

plating: Line them up on a white plate.
A few in mini paper cups like a box of chocolates.

why.0-2: A little oil keeps the chocolate fluid and gives a thinner, glossier shell.
why.0-0: Dry berries let the chocolate cling.

funFact: Chocolate-covered strawberries were popularized in Chicago in the 1960s by a confectioner named Lorraine Lorusso.
drink: Sparkling wine, or sparkling pink lemonade.
